title: Why our attention spans are shrinking, with Gloria Mark, PhD

sentences.en: When was the last time that you had an entire day completely free from digital distractions?
sentences.zh: 你上一次彻底摆脱数字干扰、度过完整的一天是什么时候？

sentences.en: No text messages, no email notifications, no social media, and no aimless internet browsing.
sentences.zh: 没有短信，没有邮件通知，没有社交媒体，也没有漫无目的的网页浏览。

sentences.en: It might be hard to think of the last time you even had a tech-free hour.
sentences.zh: 甚至很难想起你上一次哪怕度过一个小时的“无科技”时光是什么时候。

sentences.en: These days, most of us live our lives tethered to our computers and our smartphones, which are unending sources of distraction.
sentences.zh: 如今，我们大多数人的生活都离不开电脑和智能手机，它们是无休止的干扰源。

sentences.en: Sometimes it can feel impossible to concentrate deeply on anything for any significant length of time.
sentences.zh: 有时，想要长时间专注于任何事情似乎都成了不可能的任务。

sentences.en: And indeed, researchers have found evidence that over the past couple of decades, people's attention spans have shrunk considerably.
sentences.zh: 事实上，研究人员已经发现证据表明，在过去几十年里，人们的注意力持续时间已经大幅缩短。

sentences.en: So how has the rise of the internet and digital devices affected our ability to focus and pay attention?
sentences.zh: 那么，互联网和数字设备的兴起是如何影响我们专注和集中注意力的能力的呢？

sentences.en: What does it mean to pay attention to something anyway?
sentences.zh: 话说回来，所谓的“集中注意力”到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: When you're being bombarded by different tasks, notifications, and emails, is it possible to multitask and deal with them all effectively?
sentences.zh: 当你被各种任务、通知和邮件狂轰滥炸时，有可能实现多任务处理并有效地应对它们吗？

sentences.en: Or is productive multitasking a myth?
sentences.zh: 还是说，高效的多任务处理只是一个神话？

sentences.en: How can understanding the science of attention help us to regain our focus when we need it, to improve both our productivity and our happiness?
sentences.zh: 了解注意力的科学如何帮助我们在需要时重新集中注意力，从而提高我们的工作效率和幸福感？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，

sentences.en: Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Gloria Mark, a psychologist and the Chancellor's Professor of Informatics at the University of
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是格洛丽亚·马克博士，她是加州大学欧文分校的心理学家兼信息学教授。

sentences.en: California, Irvine.
sentences.zh: （接上句）加州大学欧文分校。

sentences.en: Dr. Mark studies how people interact with technology in their everyday lives and how technology affects our attention, multitasking, mood, and stress level.
sentences.zh: 马克博士研究人们在日常生活中如何与技术互动，以及技术如何影响我们的注意力、多任务处理能力、情绪和压力水平。

sentences.en: She studies people's behavior in real-world settings, and she's found that our attention spans have been shrinking over the past two decades.
sentences.zh: 她研究人们在现实环境中的行为，并发现过去二十年来我们的注意力持续时间一直在缩短。

sentences.en: Her new book published in January is called Attention Span, a groundbreaking way to restore balance, happiness, and productivity.
sentences.zh: 她一月份出版的新书名为《注意力跨度》，书中提出了一种恢复平衡、幸福感和生产力的开创性方法。

sentences.en: Dr. Mark, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 马克博士，感谢您今天接受我的采访。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Most of us probably think that we know what it means when we say we pay attention to something, but you wrote in your book that there are different kinds of attention.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人可能认为自己知道“集中注意力”是什么意思，但你在书中写道，注意力其实有不同的种类。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: What are the different kinds of attentions that we experience in our everyday life?
sentences.zh: 我们在日常生活中会经历哪些不同种类的注意力？

sentences.en: Let me actually start out by talking about what William James, the father of psychology says about attention.
sentences.zh: 其实，我想先从心理学之父威廉·詹姆斯关于注意力的论述说起。

sentences.en: So back in the 19th century, he said, everyone knows what attention is.
sentences.zh: 早在19世纪，他就说过，每个人都知道什么是注意力。

sentences.en: It's the taking possession by the mind in clear and vivid form of one out of what seems several simultaneously possible objects or trains of thought.
sentences.zh: 它是心灵以清晰生动的形式，从似乎同时存在的多个可能对象或思想链中，取其一而占有之。

sentences.en: Of course, everyone knows what attention is.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都知道什么是注意力。

sentences.en: We all believe we know what attention is.
sentences.zh: 我们都相信自己知道什么是注意力。

sentences.en: But it's a lot more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 但它远比这复杂得多。

sentences.en: So when I was studying attention, it occurred to me that you can be very engaged in something and you can put in a lot of mental effort.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我在研究注意力时，我意识到你可以在做某事时非常投入，并投入大量的脑力。

sentences.en: You know, if I'm reading an article, you know, I really have to, it can be challenging for me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我在读一篇文章，我真的必须……这对我来说可能很有挑战性。

sentences.en: On the other hand, there's a lot of things we do that are not at all challenging, but we're very engaged in.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们做的很多事情一点挑战性都没有，但我们却非常投入。

sentences.en: So when we're playing solitaire or, you know, playing simple games online, or, you know, if a person is gardening, you know, they might be very engaged and not at all challenged.
sentences.zh: 比如我们在玩纸牌游戏，或者在网上玩简单的游戏，或者如果一个人在园艺，他们可能非常投入，但一点也不觉得有挑战性。

sentences.en: So we set out to study different kinds of attention when people use their devices.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们着手研究人们使用设备时不同种类的注意力。

sentences.en: And what we did was we probed people throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是在一天中不断地对人们进行探测。

sentences.en: And we asked them, you know, at this point in time, I want you to respond very quickly and tell us how engaged were you in what you just
sentences.zh: 我们问他们，在这一刻，我希望你快速回答，告诉我们你刚才做的事情有多投入，

sentences.en: did and how challenged were you in what you just did.
sentences.zh: 以及你刚才做的事情有多大的挑战性。

sentences.en: We find that when people are engaged and challenged, there seems to be rhythms in the day when this happens.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当人们处于投入且有挑战性的状态时，一天中似乎存在着某种节奏。

sentences.en: And people seem to have peaks of times when they do this.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎在某些时段会达到这种状态的峰值。

sentences.en: We call this focused attention.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“专注的注意力”。

sentences.en: Tends to be late morning and again, mid to late afternoon, about two to three.
sentences.zh: 这往往发生在上午晚些时候，以及下午中后期，大约两三点钟。

sentences.en: And when people are very engaged in something and not at all challenged, we call that rote activity.
sentences.zh: 当人们非常投入某事但完全没有挑战性时，我们称之为“机械活动”。

sentences.en: Lots of things that people do are rote activity when they're online.
sentences.zh: 人们上网时做的很多事情都是机械活动。

sentences.en: It could be simple games.
sentences.zh: 可能是简单的游戏。

sentences.en: It could be even reading the news or doing social media.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是看新闻或刷社交媒体。

sentences.en: They tend to do that relatively uniformly throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 他们往往在一天中相对均匀地做这些事情。

sentences.en: But we do find that focused attention occurs in rhythMs. And it seems to correspond to the ebb and flow of our mental resources that we have available.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实发现，专注的注意力是有节奏地出现的。它似乎与我们可用心理资源的起伏相对应。

sentences.en: Well, I mentioned in the introduction that you have found evidence that our attention spans have shrunk
sentences.zh: 我在介绍中提到，你已经发现证据表明我们的注意力持续时间在近年来有所缩短，

sentences.en: in recent years, at least as measured by how long people spend on tasks and screens at work.
sentences.zh: 至少从人们在工作中处理任务和屏幕的时间来看是这样。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: How much have our attention spans shrunk?
sentences.zh: 我们的注意力持续时间缩短了多少？

sentences.en: So, you know, we started measuring this back in 2004.
sentences.zh: 我们是在2004年开始测量这个的。

sentences.en: And at the time, the measures that we used were stopwatches, because that was the most precise thing we had at the time, we would shadow people with stopwatches.
sentences.zh: 当时我们使用的测量工具是秒表，因为那是当时我们能拥有的最精确的东西，我们会用秒表跟踪人们。

sentences.en: For every single activity they did, we would record the start time and the stop time.
sentences.zh: 对于他们做的每一项活动，我们都会记录开始时间和结束时间。

sentences.en: So, you're on a screen where you're working in a Word doc.
sentences.zh: 比如你在屏幕上处理一个Word文档。

sentences.en: As soon as you get to that screen, we click start time.
sentences.zh: 你一进入那个屏幕，我们就点击开始时间。

sentences.en: As soon as they turned away and checked email, we clicked stop time for the Word doc and start time for the email.
sentences.zh: 他们一转头去查邮件，我们就点击Word文档的结束时间，并开始记录邮件的开始时间。

sentences.en: But fortunately,
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，

sentences.en: sophisticated computer logging methods were developed.
sentences.zh: 后来开发出了复杂的计算机日志记录方法。

sentences.en: And so, of course, we switched to those.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们当然改用了这些方法。

sentences.en: So, back in 2004, we found the average attention span on any screen to be two and a half minutes on average.
sentences.zh: 回到2004年，我们发现屏幕上的平均注意力持续时间平均为两分半钟。

sentences.en: Throughout the years, it became shorter.
sentences.zh: 多年来，它变得越来越短。

sentences.en: So, around 2012, we found it to be 75 seconds.
sentences.zh: 所以，大约在2012年，我们发现它是75秒。

sentences.en: This is with logging techniques.
sentences.zh: 这是通过日志记录技术得出的。

sentences.en: This is an average.
sentences.zh: 这是一个平均值。

sentences.en: And then in the last five, six years, we found it to average about 47 seconds.
sentences.zh: 然后在过去五六年里，我们发现平均时间约为47秒。

sentences.en: And others have replicated this result within a few seconds.
sentences.zh: 其他人也在几秒钟的误差范围内重复了这一结果。

sentences.en: So, it seems to be quite robuSt. Now, another way to think about this result is the median.
sentences.zh: 所以，这似乎相当稳健。现在，考虑这个结果的另一种方式是中位数。

sentences.en: The median means the midpoint of observations.
sentences.zh: 中位数意味着观测值的中间点。

sentences.en: The median is 40 seconds.
sentences.zh: 中位数是40秒。

sentences.en: And what this means is that half of all the measurements that we found were 40 seconds or less of people's attention spans.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们发现的所有测量结果中，有一半是40秒或更短的注意力持续时间。

sentences.en: Now, you know, obviously, because we're talking about averages and medians, sometimes people do spend longer.
sentences.zh: 当然，因为我们讨论的是平均值和中位数，有时人们确实会花费更长时间。

sentences.en: But quite a good bit of the time, their attention spans are much shorter and with an average coming to 47 seconds.
sentences.zh: 但在相当多的时间里，他们的注意力持续时间要短得多，平均只有47秒。

sentences.en: So, why is this a problem?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么这是一个问题呢？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, since it seems to be happening almost universally at this point, is this just the new normal?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，既然这在目前看来几乎是普遍发生的，这难道不是新常态吗？

sentences.en: It seems to be the new normal because we seem to have reached a steady state over the last five or six years where these are the measures that we're seeing.
sentences.zh: 这似乎确实是新常态，因为在过去五六年里，我们似乎已经达到了一个稳定状态，这就是我们看到的测量结果。

sentences.en: Is this a good thing?
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: I would argue it's not a good thing for the following reasons.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不是一件好事，原因如下。

sentences.en: First of all, we find in our research a correlation between
sentences.zh: 首先，我们在研究中发现注意力切换频率与压力之间存在相关性。

sentences.en: frequency of attention switching and stress.
sentences.zh: 注意力切换发生得越快，压力就越大，这是通过人们佩戴心率监测器测量出来的。

sentences.en: So, the faster the attention switching occurs, stress as measured by people wearing heart rate monitors.
sentences.zh: （接上句）压力就越大。

sentences.en: We show that stress goes up.
sentences.zh: 我们证明了压力会上升。

sentences.en: We know from decades of research in the laboratory that when people multitask, they experience stress.
sentences.zh: 我们从实验室几十年的研究中得知，当人们进行多任务处理时，他们会感到压力。

sentences.en: Blood pressure rises.
sentences.zh: 血压会升高。

sentences.en: There's a physiological marker in the body that indicates people are stressed.
sentences.zh: 身体里有一种生理指标表明人们处于压力之下。

sentences.en: And, you know, in our studies, we've also simply asked people with well-valid instruments to report their stress, their perceived stress.
sentences.zh: 而且，在我们的研究中，我们也简单地使用经过充分验证的工具让人们报告他们的压力，即感知压力。

sentences.en: And it's reported to be higher the faster that we measure attention shifting.
sentences.zh: 据报告，我们测量到的注意力切换越快，压力就越高。

sentences.en: So, all of these measures seem to be consistent.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些测量结果似乎都是一致的。

sentences.en: I also measure that when people shift their attention so fast, and this is multitasking when you keep switching your attention among different activities, people make more errors.
sentences.zh: 我还测量到，当人们切换注意力如此之快时——这就是当你不断在不同活动之间切换注意力时的多任务处理——人们会犯更多的错误。

sentences.en: And that's been shown in studies in the real world with physicians, nurses, pilots.
sentences.zh: 这已经在现实世界中针对医生、护士和飞行员的研究中得到了证实。

sentences.en: We also know that performance slows.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道表现会变慢。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because there's something called a switch coSt. So, every time you switch your attention, you have to reorient to that new activity,
sentences.zh: 因为有一种东西叫做“切换成本”。所以，每次你切换注意力，你都必须重新定向到那个新活动，

sentences.en: that new thing you're paying attention to, and it takes a little bit of time.
sentences.zh: 那个你正在关注的新事物，这需要一点时间。

sentences.en: So, imagine if you're
sentences.zh: 所以，想象一下如果你正在

sentences.en: writing, let's say, you're writing a chapter, and you suddenly stop what you're doing, and you switch and do something else, and then you come back to it.
sentences.zh: 写作，比如说，你正在写一章，突然你停下手中的工作，切换去做别的事情，然后再回来。

sentences.en: It's going to take you some time to reconstruct, you know, what was I writing?
sentences.zh: 你需要一些时间来重构，你知道，我刚才写到哪了？

sentences.en: You know, what was the topic I was thinking about?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我刚才在思考什么主题？

sentences.en: What were the words I was using?
sentences.zh: 我刚才用了什么词？

sentences.en: That takes a bit of time.
sentences.zh: 这需要一点时间。

sentences.en: And so, we incur these switch costs throughout the day as we're switching our attention.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们切换注意力时，我们全天都在承担这些切换成本。

sentences.en: And, you know, this creates more effort.
sentences.zh: 而且，这会产生更多的努力。

sentences.en: It uses more of our very precious mental resources on top of the work that we actually need to do.
sentences.zh: 除了我们实际需要做的工作之外，它还消耗了我们更多宝贵的心理资源。

sentences.en: You've also found that some switching is good.
sentences.zh: 你也发现有些切换是有益的。

sentences.en: It's normal during the course of a day so that you might really concentrate on something for a length of time, and then you take a break.
sentences.zh: 在一天中这是正常的，这样你可能会真正专注于某件事一段时间，然后休息一下。

sentences.en: And maybe you go online, or maybe if you're working from home, you put in a load of laundry, or you take a walk.
sentences.zh: 也许你上网，或者如果你在家工作，你洗了一堆衣服，或者去散步。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't that something that we actually need to do?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这难道不是我们真正需要做的事情吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: It's so important that we take breaks, because if you work until you get exhausted, then, of course, you can get burnt out.
sentences.zh: 休息非常重要，因为如果你工作到精疲力竭，那么当然，你可能会倦怠。

sentences.en: It's so important to take breaks and replenish.
sentences.zh: 休息和补充能量非常重要。

sentences.en: And by taking breaks, we have more energy, we have more attentional capacity, and we can actually do more.
sentences.zh: 通过休息，我们有了更多的精力，更多的注意力容量，我们实际上可以做得更多。

sentences.en: We can be more productive.
sentences.zh: 我们可以更有效率。

sentences.en: The problem is that in our current world, many work environments, people neglect to take meaningful breaks.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，在我们当今的世界里，许多工作环境中，人们忽略了进行有意义的休息。

sentences.en: And, you know, we get ourselves into a position where we end up having our performance suffers as a result.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们让自己陷入了一种境地，最终导致我们的表现因此受损。

sentences.en: Now, if you're going to take a break, it's really important to take a break at a point in the task that's called a break point.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你要休息，在任务中所谓的“断点”处休息非常重要。

sentences.en: And a break point is a natural stopping point in a task.
sentences.zh: 断点是任务中的自然停止点。

sentences.en: So going back to the writing example, if I'm writing something, a break point would be at the end of a section, or even at the end of a paragraph, right?
sentences.zh: 回到写作的例子，如果我正在写东西，断点会在一个章节的末尾，甚至是一个段落的末尾，对吧？

sentences.en: But at a point where when I come back to it, then there's not going to be a lot of effort for me to have to reconstruct what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 但在那个点上，当我回来时，我不需要花费太大的努力去重构我刚才在做什么。

sentences.en: I've already finished that part.
sentences.zh: 我已经完成了那部分。

sentences.en: If you interrupt yourself in the middle of doing something as opposed to a natural stopping point, you use up a lot more mental resources, and it's also more stressful.
sentences.zh: 如果你在做某事的过程中打断自己，而不是在自然停止点，你会消耗更多的心理资源，而且压力也更大。

sentences.en: Well, for people who want to schedule breaks, who really want to intentionally make the changes that
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那些想要安排休息时间，真正想要有意识地做出你所说的改变的人，

sentences.en: you're talking about, what do you think about programs such as internet blockers that prevent
sentences.zh: 你如何看待诸如互联网拦截器之类的程序，它们可以防止

sentences.en: people from going online during certain hours of the day so that you can force yourself to be more focused?
sentences.zh: 人们在一天中的某些时段上网，这样你就可以强迫自己更加专注？

sentences.en: Do you think that those are effective?
sentences.zh: 你认为这些有效吗？

sentences.en: We've done a study with internet blockers, and it turns out it very much depends on an individual's personality.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一项关于互联网拦截器的研究，结果发现这很大程度上取决于个人的性格。

sentences.en: So people who have poor self-regulation skills can benefit from these kinds of blockers.
sentences.zh: 所以，自我调节能力差的人可以从这些拦截器中受益。

sentences.en: You know, essentially what you're doing is you're offloading the work of self-regulation onto the software, and the software becomes a proxy agent for you, right?
sentences.zh: 本质上，你所做的是将自我调节的工作卸载给软件，软件成为了你的代理人，对吧？

sentences.en: It's doing the work.
sentences.zh: 它在替你工作。

sentences.en: It turns out people who have good self-regulation skills, so people who score low in impulsivity
sentences.zh: 事实证明，自我调节能力强的人，即冲动性得分较低的人，

sentences.en: as a trade, people who score high in conscientiousness, these are people who are actually harmed by these blockers.
sentences.zh: 责任心得分较高的人，这些人实际上会受到这些拦截器的伤害。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because these are people who are very good at taking breaks and coming right back to work.
sentences.zh: 因为这些人非常擅长休息并立即回到工作中。

sentences.en: They can take a break, they can go to social media, they can go to a news site,
sentences.zh: 他们可以休息，可以去社交媒体，可以去新闻网站，

sentences.en: and they can take a break, relax themselves, then they can come back to work.
sentences.zh: 他们可以休息一下，放松自己，然后回到工作中。

sentences.en: In this study, we took away their opportunity to take a quick online break, and they got burned out.
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，我们剥夺了他们进行快速在线休息的机会，结果他们倦怠了。

sentences.en: They worked straight through.
sentences.zh: 他们一直工作到底。

sentences.en: They didn't take breaks.
sentences.zh: 他们没有休息。

sentences.en: On the whole, I prefer that people develop their own agency, their own self-efficacy in controlling their attention.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我更希望人们培养自己的能动性，培养自己在控制注意力方面的自我效能感。

sentences.en: You know, these software blockers
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些软件拦截器

sentences.en: can be good at times, but I think it's far more important that people learn to develop their own skills to control their attention.
sentences.zh: 有时可能有用，但我认为更重要的是人们学会培养自己控制注意力的技能。

sentences.en: You know, a lot has been written about the Pomodoro technique, which is basically, you set a timer for every 25 minutes to do, and then you agree you're going to
sentences.zh: 关于番茄工作法，人们已经写了很多，基本上就是你设定一个25分钟的计时器，然后你同意

sentences.en: work straight through for 25 minutes, the timer goes off, and you get a five-minute break.
sentences.zh: 连续工作25分钟，计时器响了，你就休息五分钟。

sentences.en: What about that as sort of a low-tech blocker?
sentences.zh: 把这作为一种低科技的拦截器怎么样？

sentences.en: Well, that's fine, but there are individual differences.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那很好，但存在个体差异。

sentences.en: And, you know, some people would be able to work longer than what the Pomodoro technique dictates.
sentences.zh: 有些人能够工作的时间比番茄工作法规定的要长。

sentences.en: Some people would work less.
sentences.zh: 有些人工作的时间会更短。

sentences.en: I think it's much more important that people become self-aware of their own level of energy and the amount of attentional resources they have available,
sentences.zh: 我认为更重要的是，人们要对自己拥有的能量水平和可用注意力资源量有自我意识，

sentences.en: and take breaks according to what their own levels are.
sentences.zh: 并根据自己的水平进行休息。

sentences.en: So, you know, I've learned to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以，我已经学会了这样做。

sentences.en: I've learned to become more aware of what my own capacity is.
sentences.zh: 我已经学会了更加留意自己的能力极限。

sentences.en: And when I start feeling tired, that's the point when I take a break.
sentences.zh: 当我开始感到疲惫时，那就是我该休息的时候了。

sentences.en: If I know I've got a really hard task to do, I might schedule a break before I start doing that task so I can replenish myself, and then right after,
sentences.zh: 如果我知道有一项非常艰巨的任务要完成，我可能会在开始之前就安排好休息时间，以便让自己恢复精力，然后在任务结束后，

sentences.en: that I can build back up the resources that I expended.
sentences.zh: 我能够补充回我所消耗的资源。

sentences.en: The worst thing you can do, the worst thing is to schedule back-to-back Zoom meetings without breaks, that it just gets us exhausted.
sentences.zh: 你能做的最糟糕的事情，最糟糕的事情就是安排连续不断的 Zoom 会议而不留休息时间，这只会让我们精疲力竭。

sentences.en: There's no transition between these meetings.
sentences.zh: 这些会议之间没有任何过渡。

sentences.en: So, we need to schedule in transitions between these kinds of hard tasks.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们需要在这些艰巨的任务之间安排过渡时间。

sentences.en: And when we're talking about attention and attention spans, there's something a little bit different but related, which is the concept of flow.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论注意力和注意力持续时间时，有一个略有不同但相关联的概念，那就是“心流”。

sentences.en: Can you explain what that is?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下那是什么吗？

sentences.en: Because that is a kind of attention, and it's very, very different from what we've just been talking about.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一种注意力，而且它与我们刚才讨论的内容非常、非常不同。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, flow is a type of attention that the psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi discovered.
sentences.zh: 心流是心理学家米哈里·契克森米哈赖发现的一种注意力类型。

sentences.en: And it's what he calls the optimal state of attention.
sentences.zh: 他将其称为注意力的最佳状态。

sentences.en: It's when people are so immersed in something that time just doesn't seem to matter.
sentences.zh: 在这种状态下，人们沉浸在某件事中，以至于时间似乎都失去了意义。

sentences.en: And so, it's when we are at our peak creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我们创造力达到巅峰的时候。

sentences.en: We're using the optimal amount of challenge of our skills.
sentences.zh: 我们正在以最佳的挑战程度来运用我们的技能。

sentences.en: So, if we're not challenged enough in whatever your skill happens to be, you won't go into flow.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在某项技能上没有受到足够的挑战，你就不会进入心流状态。

sentences.en: If you're challenged too much in your skill, you won't go into flow.
sentences.zh: 如果你在某项技能上受到的挑战太大，你也不会进入心流状态。

sentences.en: It'll be too hard.
sentences.zh: 那会太难了。

sentences.en: So, there's that sweet spot that you have to hit to go into flow.
sentences.zh: 所以，要进入心流状态，必须达到那个“甜蜜点”。

sentences.en: So, before I went into psychology, I actually had studied fine arts and used to be an artist, and I would get into flow regularly.
sentences.zh: 在进入心理学领域之前，我其实学过美术，也曾是一名艺术家，我经常能进入心流状态。

sentences.en: And it's the nature of the work of, you know, being an artist and, you know, being creative that I could regularly get into flow.
sentences.zh: 作为一名艺术家，从事创造性工作，这种工作的本质让我能够经常进入心流状态。

sentences.en: Now, as a scientist,
sentences.zh: 现在，作为一名科学家，

sentences.en: I rarely get into flow because of the nature of my work where I have to be very analytical.
sentences.zh: 我很少进入心流状态，因为我的工作性质要求我必须进行高度的分析。

sentences.en: And I have, you know, I have to use very careful thought.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须进行非常谨慎的思考。

sentences.en: Is that a bad thing?
sentences.zh: 这是一件坏事吗？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是。

sentences.en: It's very rewarding.
sentences.zh: 这非常有成就感。

sentences.en: It's just, I realize that the nature of my work and the nature of a lot of knowledge work is such that it may not be conducive to flow.
sentences.zh: 只是我意识到，我的工作性质以及许多知识型工作的性质，可能并不利于产生心流。

sentences.en: But sometimes I get into flow if I'm in, say, a brainstorming session with other people.
sentences.zh: 但有时如果我参加比如与他人的头脑风暴会议，我也会进入心流状态。

sentences.en: We might get into a kind of group flow where, you know, we're just, everyone is feeding off of each other's ideas.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会进入一种“群体心流”，每个人都在汲取彼此的想法。

sentences.en: But, you know, in my typical day-to-day life now, I generally don't get into flow.
sentences.zh: 但是，在我现在典型的日常生活中，我通常不会进入心流状态。

sentences.en: And it's not a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一件坏事。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about the effect of the internet and devices on children's attention span.
sentences.zh: 让我们花点时间谈谈互联网和电子设备对儿童注意力持续时间的影响。

sentences.en: Most of your research has been with adults, but kids are spending a lot of time on devices as well.
sentences.zh: 你的大部分研究对象是成年人，但孩子们也在电子设备上花费了大量时间。

sentences.en: Are they going to have even more trouble with attention than those of us who first experienced this level of distraction as adults?
sentences.zh: 与我们这些成年后才第一次经历这种程度干扰的人相比，他们是否会面临更严重的注意力问题？

sentences.en: This is something that I think we should be very concerned about as a society.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一个社会，我们应该对此感到非常担忧。

sentences.en: So it turns out children that are as young as two to four years old, they already average two and a half hours of screen time a day.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，两到四岁的儿童平均每天已经有两到两个半小时的屏幕时间。

sentences.en: And when they get to be between five and eight, they average about three hours of screen time a day.
sentences.zh: 而当他们长到五到八岁时，平均每天的屏幕时间约为三小时。

sentences.en: Now, most of that screen time, it's TV and YouTube viewing.
sentences.zh: 现在，大部分屏幕时间都是在看电视和 YouTube。

sentences.en: But children also do a lot of gaming, right?
sentences.zh: 但孩子们也玩很多游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: So we know from a lot of laboratory studies that when children are very young, they're a lot more susceptible to distraction than older children.
sentences.zh: 我们从许多实验室研究中得知，当孩子还很小时，他们比大一点的孩子更容易受到干扰。

sentences.en: And when they're distracted, it takes them longer to get back and focus again on that thing that they were distracted from.
sentences.zh: 而且当他们分心时，他们需要更长的时间才能重新回到之前专注的事情上。

sentences.en: So, you know, I worry that when young children are spending so much time on the screen, it acculturates them to think that this is normal behavior to be on a screen.
sentences.zh: 所以，我担心当幼儿花这么多时间在屏幕上时，这会让他们习惯性地认为盯着屏幕是正常行为。

sentences.en: The problem is that when children are very young, there are certain parts of their brain that are not yet mature.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当孩子还很小时，他们大脑的某些部分尚未成熟。

sentences.en: So their ability to self-control and a part of the brain called executive function.
sentences.zh: 比如他们的自我控制能力，以及大脑中被称为“执行功能”的部分。

sentences.en: And executive function is, you can think of it as the governor of the mind.
sentences.zh: 你可以把执行功能想象成大脑的“管理者”。

sentences.en: So it manages things like decision-making and setting priorities of what we should be paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 它管理着决策和设定优先级等事务，决定我们应该关注什么。

sentences.en: It helps manage interference of peripheral stimuli in the environment.
sentences.zh: 它有助于管理环境中外围刺激的干扰。

sentences.en: And executive function is not yet well-developed and children are sitting in front of screens and they're exposed to all kinds of potential distractions.
sentences.zh: 而当执行功能尚未发育完善时，孩子们坐在屏幕前，就会接触到各种潜在的干扰。

sentences.en: So I think this is not a good idea.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这不是个好主意。

sentences.en: Children need self-control.
sentences.zh: 孩子们需要自我控制能力。

sentences.en: For learning.
sentences.zh: 为了学习。

sentences.en: And more and more, we're seeing schools having a lot of online learning available for kids.
sentences.zh: 而且我们越来越多地看到学校为孩子们提供了大量的在线学习资源。

sentences.en: And kids need self-control as a skill to be able to search for information, to do math problems online, to read and write without being distracted.
sentences.zh: 孩子们需要自我控制作为一种技能，才能在不分心的情况下搜索信息、做在线数学题、阅读和写作。

sentences.en: I find it problematic that we're putting children into a digital world before some very critical mental functions are fully developed.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在一些关键的心理功能完全发育成熟之前，就让孩子们进入数字世界是有问题的。

sentences.en: I don't think kids are really ready for that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为孩子们真的准备好了。

sentences.en: Can focus be taught?
sentences.zh: 专注力可以被训练吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you seem to be implying that we need to be doing something, particularly with children, so that they aren't constantly distracted.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你似乎在暗示我们需要采取一些行动，特别是针对儿童，这样他们就不会总是分心。

sentences.en: But I mean, how do you teach somebody to focus on something?
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，你如何教一个人专注于某件事？

sentences.en: Well, for children, I think the best thing children can do is to do activity off screen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于孩子来说，我认为他们能做的最好的事情就是进行屏幕之外的活动。

sentences.en: And I think they would learn to focus, whether it's, you know, playing outside, reading books is an excellent way to get children to focus.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们会学会专注，无论是去户外玩耍，还是阅读书籍，都是让孩子学会专注的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: If we're talking about adults, I think that one of the best things that adults can do is to make sure that your internal tank of mental resources is kept at a high capacity.
sentences.zh: 如果我们谈论的是成年人，我认为成年人能做的最好的事情之一，就是确保你内心的心理资源储备保持在高水平。

sentences.en: So when you have a full tank of resources, you can focus much better than when you're just spent, you know, when your resources have just
sentences.zh: 所以，当你拥有充足的资源储备时，你的专注力会比你精疲力竭时好得多，你知道，当你的资源已经

sentences.en: drained, because you're doing hard work all day, you're switching your attention a lot, it's going to be very, very hard to focus.
sentences.zh: 耗尽时，因为你整天都在做艰苦的工作，频繁切换注意力，想要专注会变得非常非常困难。

sentences.en: And, and there are things we can do to build up those resources.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们确实可以做一些事情来积累这些资源。

sentences.en: So we can, one of the best things you can do is to get a really good night's sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以，你能做的最好的事情之一就是保证充足的睡眠。

sentences.en: I know, everyone says, of course, we know you should get a good night's sleep.
sentences.zh: 我知道，每个人都说，当然，我们知道你应该保证充足的睡眠。

sentences.en: But let me tell you what happens when you don't.
sentences.zh: 但让我告诉你当你睡眠不足时会发生什么。

sentences.en: When, when people accumulate what's called sleep debt, and sleep debt is the accumulation of loss of sleep.
sentences.zh: 当人们积累了所谓的“睡眠债”，而睡眠债就是睡眠不足的累积。

sentences.en: If you need eight hours of sleep a night, and I need eight hours of sleep a night.
sentences.zh: 如果你每晚需要八小时睡眠，我也需要八小时睡眠。

sentences.en: But if you're only getting six hours a night, that difference is called a sleep debt.
sentences.zh: 但如果你每晚只睡六小时，那个差额就叫睡眠债。

sentences.en: And if you're consistently getting six hours of sleep a night, you're accumulating sleep debt.
sentences.zh: 如果你持续每晚只睡六小时，你就在不断积累睡眠债。

sentences.en: And we know that the greater the sleep debt, the shorter the attention spans.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，睡眠债越多，注意力持续时间就越短。

sentences.en: And what do people do when they have a lot of sleep debt?
sentences.zh: 当人们背负大量睡眠债时会做什么？

sentences.en: We found that they tend to do more lightweight activities like social media.
sentences.zh: 我们发现他们倾向于做一些更轻松的活动，比如刷社交媒体。

sentences.en: They just don't have the resources to be able to focus and do hard work.
sentences.zh: 他们只是没有足够的资源来集中精力做艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: So they, they do what's easy based on the amount of resources that they have available.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会根据自己现有的资源量，选择做一些容易的事情。

sentences.en: Let's switch topics for a minute to something else that you talk about in your book, which is how TV and movies have changed in the past few decades.
sentences.zh: 让我们换个话题，谈谈你在书中提到的另一件事，即电视和电影在过去几十年里是如何变化的。

sentences.en: You write that the pace of television and movies has sped up and things like the length of each camera shot, they're getting shorter.
sentences.zh: 你写道，电视和电影的节奏加快了，比如每个镜头的长度都在变短。

sentences.en: Um, why is that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么会这样？

sentences.en: And are those changes affecting our attention?
sentences.zh: 这些变化是否正在影响我们的注意力？

sentences.en: Or is this happening because the people who are creating these things already know that we have no attention anymore?
sentences.zh: 还是因为创作这些内容的人已经知道我们不再有注意力了，所以才发生这种情况？

sentences.en: So I, I was very surprised to learn that TV and film shot lengths have decreased over the years.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶地发现，多年来电视和电影的镜头长度确实在缩短。

sentences.en: Um, they started out much longer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们最初要长得多。

sentences.en: They now average about four seconds, a shot like that's on average.
sentences.zh: 现在平均每个镜头大约只有四秒钟。

sentences.en: If you watch, uh, MTV music videos, they're much shorter.
sentences.zh: 如果你看 MTV 音乐录影带，它们会更短。

sentences.en: They're only a couple of seconds.
sentences.zh: 只有几秒钟。

sentences.en: So very, we're, we've become accustomed to seeing very fast shot lengths when we look at TV and film.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经习惯了在看电视和电影时看到非常快速的镜头切换。

sentences.en: Uh, even commercials have shortened in length.
sentences.zh: 甚至商业广告的长度也缩短了。

sentences.en: Commercials used to be much longer.
sentences.zh: 商业广告过去要长得多。

sentences.en: Now it's not uncommon to see six second commercials, even shorter than that.
sentences.zh: 现在看到六秒钟的广告，甚至更短的广告，已经不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Now it's a chicken and egg question.
sentences.zh: 现在这是一个“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的问题。

sentences.en: We don't know if TV and film have affected our attention spans on computers and phones.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道是电视和电影影响了我们在电脑和手机上的注意力持续时间。

sentences.en: We don't know if our attention spans have affected the decision-making of film editors and, uh, and directors.
sentences.zh: 还是我们的注意力持续时间影响了电影剪辑师和导演的决策。

sentences.en: We, we don't know exactly if there is any causal connection.
sentences.zh: 我们并不确切知道是否存在任何因果联系。

sentences.en: We see these two parallel trends.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了这两个平行的趋势。

sentences.en: It could, it could be the case that directors and editors are influenced by their own short
sentences.zh: 可能是导演和剪辑师在创作这些电影镜头时，受到了他们自己短暂的

sentences.en: attention spans when they create these film shots, or it could be that they're creating short film shots because they think that's what the viewer wants to see.
sentences.zh: 注意力持续时间的影响，也可能是因为他们认为观众想看短镜头，所以才创作了短镜头。

sentences.en: But, uh, but this has become quite ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况已经变得相当普遍了。

sentences.en: In fact, uh, on YouTube, uh, there's a particular YouTube aesthetic, which uses jump cuts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在 YouTube 上，有一种特定的 YouTube 美学，它使用了“跳剪”。

sentences.en: So when you're watching a YouTube film, the film becomes very jumpy, right?
sentences.zh: 所以当你观看 YouTube 视频时，画面会变得非常跳跃，对吧？

sentences.en: It's the natural pauses that people make when they speak is removed.
sentences.zh: 人们说话时的自然停顿被删除了。

sentences.en: So the idea is to pack more content into a shorter amount of time.
sentences.zh: 所以其目的是在更短的时间内塞入更多的内容。

sentences.en: So, you know, we're seeing short lengths of content from all directions.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正从各个方向看到短小精悍的内容。

sentences.en: It's not just what we're attending to on computers and phones.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是我们关注电脑和手机时的情况。

sentences.en: But I think you found that some of this we're doing to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你发现其中一些是我们自己造成的。

sentences.en: Like I know some people who feel like they're so time crunched that when they want to listen to a podcast, they turn up the speed to 1.5 or two, you know, and then listen to it.
sentences.zh: 比如我认识一些人，他们觉得时间太紧迫，以至于想听播客时，会把速度调到 1.5 倍或 2 倍，然后去听。

sentences.en: I mean, why are we doing this to ourselves?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们为什么要对自己这样做？

sentences.en: And is this helping?
sentences.zh: 这有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Uh, you know, I myself have sometimes done that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我自己有时也会这样做。

sentences.en: Why do we do this?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: Uh, you know, there's a number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，原因有很多。

sentences.en: I can't say exactly why we do.
sentences.zh: 我不能确切地说为什么。

sentences.en: It could be because we want to fit more content into a shorter amount of time because there's so much content available, right?
sentences.zh: 可能是因为我们想在更短的时间内塞入更多内容，因为可用的内容太多了，对吧？

sentences.en: We're talking about access to the world's largest candy store and we want to sample all the wares that are available.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是进入世界上最大的糖果店，我们想品尝所有可用的商品。

sentences.en: So of course you might want to speed up the podcast so that you can simply take more in and quickly get to your next favorite podcaSt. So, um, I, I don't know
sentences.zh: 所以你当然可能想加快播客的速度，这样你就可以简单地吸收更多内容，并快速进入下一个你喜欢的播客。所以，嗯，我不知道

sentences.en: exactly why we're doing it on ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要对自己这样做。

sentences.en: It could be also out of habit.
sentences.zh: 也可能是出于习惯。

sentences.en: We're just used to, uh, listening to things faster, but, uh, we do have, you know, all of this content available to us at our fingertips within milliseconds.
sentences.zh: 我们只是习惯了以更快的速度听东西，但我们确实拥有所有这些触手可及的内容，几毫秒内就能获取。

sentences.en: And so, you know, perhaps we just want to sample as much as we possibly can.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许我们只是想尽可能多地尝试。

sentences.en: Now, during the pandemic, many people have switched to remote work, which I'm guessing
sentences.zh: 在疫情期间，许多人转向了远程办公，我猜

sentences.en: has meant more emails, more messages on Slack and teams and workers have to deal with all of this.
sentences.zh: 这意味着更多的电子邮件、更多的 Slack 和 Teams 消息，员工必须处理所有这些信息。

sentences.en: How do you think this is affecting people's attention and focus?
sentences.zh: 你认为这如何影响人们的注意力和专注力？

sentences.en: Do, do you even know, is it too soon to say?
sentences.zh: 你甚至知道吗？现在下结论还为时过早吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I, I've worked on a survey with colleagues.
sentences.zh: 我和同事们进行了一项调查。

sentences.en: So we, we have people's self reports.
sentences.zh: 我们收集了人们的自我报告。

sentences.en: They, they reported that it's hard to focus.
sentences.zh: 他们报告说很难集中注意力。

sentences.en: I've done other work where we're looking at, uh, team, team, team interaction, uh, in remote work and, uh, have picked up some information from that.
sentences.zh: 我还做过其他研究，观察远程工作中的团队互动，并从中获取了一些信息。

sentences.en: Uh, people do report having a hard time focusing.
sentences.zh: 人们确实报告说很难集中注意力。

sentences.en: It's a different kind of distraction than you would have in a workplace.
sentences.zh: 这与你在工作场所遇到的干扰不同。

sentences.en: Uh, of course you're distracted by the pile of dirty laundry that you're looking at in a workplace.
sentences.zh: 当然，你在工作场所会被你看到的成堆脏衣服所干扰。

sentences.en: You might be, uh, distracted by ambient noise in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 你可能会被工作场所的环境噪音所干扰。

sentences.en: We, we, we do know that it makes a difference whether people have a private workspace at home
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道，人们在家中是否有私人工作空间，

sentences.en: where it can be quiet or whether they have to share a public working space with others, which is more distracting.
sentences.zh: 或者是否必须与他人共享公共工作空间，这会有所不同，后者更容易分心。

sentences.en: Uh, some people might go to a cafe to work.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会去咖啡馆工作。

sentences.en: And of course that creates another, uh, type of distraction.
sentences.zh: 当然，这会产生另一种干扰。

sentences.en: So a lot of it very much depends on the environment where the person is working.
sentences.zh: 所以很大程度上取决于个人工作的环境。

sentences.en: Um, we also know that, uh, you know, if you're remote from your colleagues, you, you can't really signal to them when is a good time to interrupt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们也知道，如果你与同事远程办公，你真的无法向他们发出信号，告知什么时候是打扰的好时机。

sentences.en: If you're in a workplace and especially if you can see your colleagues, you can see when they just hung up the phone, then you know, it might be a nice
sentences.zh: 如果你在工作场所，特别是如果你能看到同事，你可以看到他们刚挂断电话，那么你就知道，这可能是一个

sentences.en: time to walk over and talk to them, or you might stand outside their office and wait, and then you can see when it's good to interrupt.
sentences.zh: 走过去和他们交谈的好时机，或者你可以站在他们办公室外等待，然后你可以看到什么时候适合打扰。

sentences.en: Uh, when, when we're remote, we don't have that visual information.
sentences.zh: 当我们远程办公时，我们没有那种视觉信息。

sentences.en: And so we can just be sending electronic communications to our colleagues at all time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会一直向同事发送电子通讯。

sentences.en: Uh, there's another study, uh, that I did with my postdoc and she found that a lot of people
sentences.zh: 我和我的博士后做了另一项研究，她发现很多人

sentences.en: feel that they want to go above and beyond what they ordinarily do to be able to signal
sentences.zh: 觉得他们想要超越常规，以便向同事、向主管发出信号，

sentences.en: to their colleagues, to their, uh, supervisors that they're working hard.
sentences.zh: 表明他们工作很努力。

sentences.en: And so they jump to answer their email, their Slack message messages so that they can demonstrate, Hey, I'm working,
sentences.zh: 所以他们会跳出来回复电子邮件、Slack 消息，以便证明：嘿，我在工作，

sentences.en: you know, you don't see me, but I want you to know that I'm here and I'm working hard.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你看不到我，但我希望你知道我在这里，而且工作很努力。

sentences.en: And that's why I'm going to jump on these messages.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我会急于回复这些消息。

sentences.en: Now we've been talking a lot about, um, what individuals can do, uh, regarding, uh, better
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈了很多关于个人能做些什么来改善注意力持续时间的问题，但是，组织层面是否应该做出改变，或者在社会层面是否也应该做出改变，来帮助我们所有人提升专注于重要事务的能力呢？

sentences.en: attention spans, but, um, are there changes that organizations should be making or even changes
sentences.zh: 组织层面是否应该做出改变，或者在社会层面是否也应该做出改变

sentences.en: at a societal level that could help all of us with, uh, you know, sort of boosting our ability to stay focused on important things?
sentences.zh: 来帮助我们所有人提升专注于重要事务的能力呢？

sentences.en: There, there are, and I'm, I'm a big advocate for changes on a collective level.
sentences.zh: 确实有，而且我非常支持在集体层面进行变革。

sentences.en: And the reason is that if any individual decides to just, you know, pull out and completely cut themselves off from technology, um, they might penalize themselves.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，如果任何个人决定仅仅是退出并完全切断与科技的联系，他们可能会让自己处于不利地位。

sentences.en: If, if you're a knowledge worker of any kind, you're cutting yourself off from important work communications.
sentences.zh: 如果你是任何类型的知识工作者，你就会切断与重要工作沟通的联系。

sentences.en: Uh, you can be cutting yourself off from communications, from family, friends, loved ones, uh, from important news in the world.
sentences.zh: 你可能会切断与家人、朋友、爱人的沟通，以及与世界上重要新闻的联系。

sentences.en: So it's, it's not always beneficial for any individual to cut themselves off, but an organization can do things.
sentences.zh: 所以，对个人而言，切断联系并不总是有益的，但组织可以采取一些行动。

sentences.en: They can, for example, control uh, times during the day when electronic communications are set.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们可以控制一天中发送电子通讯的时间。

sentences.en: They can create a window of time when no communications would be sent.
sentences.zh: 他们可以设定一个不发送任何通讯的时间窗口。

sentences.en: And this would be a quiet time with, you know, people can work.
sentences.zh: 这段时间可以作为安静时间，让人们能够专心工作。

sentences.en: Uh, in our research, we find that people check email on average 77 times a day.
sentences.zh: 在我们的研究中，我们发现人们平均每天查看电子邮件77次。

sentences.en: And if you have this quiet time, at least you, you can curtail that, that, that checking, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你有这段安静时间，至少你可以减少那种查看的频率，对吧？

sentences.en: We might be able to reduce the amount of checking because you know, there's no point to check.
sentences.zh: 我们或许能够减少查看的次数，因为你知道，查看也没有意义。

sentences.en: There won't be email coming.
sentences.zh: 因为不会有邮件发过来。

sentences.en: On a societal level, there's starting to be what's called right to disconnect laws.
sentences.zh: 在社会层面，开始出现所谓的“离线权”法律。

sentences.en: And there's, there's, uh, one in France, it's called the El Camry law.
sentences.zh: 法国就有一项这样的法律，叫做《埃尔·库姆里法》（El Khomri law）。

sentences.en: Uh, there's, uh, also Ireland and Ontario have policies.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰和安大略省也有相关的政策。

sentences.en: So other, other countries are starting to pick up on this.
sentences.zh: 所以其他国家也开始关注这一点了。

sentences.en: And it's the idea that no worker can be penalized if they do not answer electronic communications after work hours, before and after work hours.
sentences.zh: 其核心理念是，任何员工在工作时间之外，即工作时间之前和之后，如果不回复电子通讯，都不应受到惩罚。

sentences.en: Uh, New York City tried to introduce a right to disconnect law in its city council meeting, uh, that got shut down very quickly.
sentences.zh: 纽约市曾在市议会会议上试图引入一项“离线权”法律，但很快就被否决了。

sentences.en: And my, my favorite, I read the transcripts of the meeting and my favorite response, my favorite
sentences.zh: 我读过那次会议的记录，我最喜欢的一个反对理由，

sentences.en: argument against it was, uh, from the Bureau of Tourism, which said, you know, we're the greatest tourist city in the world.
sentences.zh: 来自旅游局，他们说，我们是世界上最伟大的旅游城市。

sentences.en: We're the city that never sleeps.
sentences.zh: 我们是永不眠的城市。

sentences.en: So, you know, if, if we have right to disconnect laws, it enables people to detach from work.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们有了“离线权”法律，它能让人们从工作中抽离出来。

sentences.en: And that's, has so much psychological benefit for individuals.
sentences.zh: 这对个人有巨大的心理益处。

sentences.en: You, you truly do need a break from work.
sentences.zh: 你确实需要从工作中休息一下。

sentences.en: We, we can't be on work, uh, 24,
sentences.zh: 我们不能一直处于工作状态，

sentences.en: 24, seven.
sentences.zh: 全天候24小时。

sentences.en: And that's, that's, that's what's happening.
sentences.zh: 而这正是目前正在发生的情况。

sentences.en: The, the borders between our personal life and work life have just blurred so that, you know, in personal time, when people are at home
sentences.zh: 个人生活和工作生活之间的界限已经变得模糊，以至于人们在下班后的个人时间里，

sentences.en: after work, they're, they're dealing with work problems and work communications.
sentences.zh: 还在处理工作问题和工作沟通。

sentences.en: People do need time to really relax, to break away from work.
sentences.zh: 人们确实需要时间来真正放松，从工作中解脱出来。

sentences.en: It's, it's such a great psychological benefit.
sentences.zh: 这有着巨大的心理益处。

sentences.en: And if they can do that, it enables them to better reattach, reattach to work the next day because they're fresh, they're replenished.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能做到这一点，就能让他们在第二天更好地重新投入工作，因为他们精力充沛，得到了恢复。

sentences.en: So I'm a, I'm a big advocate of right to disconnect policy.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常支持“离线权”政策。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask you a totally different question, which is what's next for you?
sentences.zh: 那么，让我问你一个完全不同的问题，你接下来的计划是什么？

sentences.en: What are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 你现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: What are the important research questions that you want to see answered?
sentences.zh: 你希望看到哪些重要的研究问题得到解答？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So I would like to continue, uh, looking at our attention.
sentences.zh: 我想继续关注我们的注意力问题。

sentences.en: Uh, I'm interested in a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 我对很多事情都很感兴趣。

sentences.en: I'm interested in, um, how we can get more value from the internet.
sentences.zh: 我感兴趣的是，我们如何能从互联网中获得更多价值。

sentences.en: We have this incredible resource available to us.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有这样一个不可思议的资源。

sentences.en: And so rather than be, uh, upset by it because it distracts us, how can we turn that around and instead find value from it?
sentences.zh: 所以，与其因为它分散我们的注意力而感到沮丧，我们如何扭转局面，从中发现价值呢？

sentences.en: And how can we utilize our time best and optimize our time best when, when we use the resources that the internet offers without, without getting, um, exhausted from it.
sentences.zh: 当我们使用互联网提供的资源时，如何才能最好地利用和优化我们的时间，而不会因此感到精疲力竭。

sentences.en: Uh, and I also have been looking at, uh, teamwork, uh, remote teamwork, uh, and, um, how that can
sentences.zh: 此外，我一直在研究团队合作，特别是远程团队合作，以及如何对其进行优化，

sentences.en: be optimized, you know, because more and more, uh, companies are starting to have hybrid work and remote work.
sentences.zh: 因为越来越多的公司开始采用混合办公和远程办公模式。

sentences.en: And what, what are the repercussions from that?
sentences.zh: 这会带来什么影响？

sentences.en: What are the benefits from that?
sentences.zh: 这又有什么好处？

sentences.en: So I'd like to, uh, understand that better.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望能更深入地了解这些。

sentences.en: Well, that all sounds really interesting.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实非常有趣。

sentences.en: I look forward to, uh, seeing your subsequent research.
sentences.zh: 我很期待看到你后续的研究成果。

sentences.en: I appreciate your joining me today, Dr. Mark.
sentences.zh: 感谢你今天参加我们的节目，马克博士。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我参加。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org 或 Apple、Stitcher 以及您获取播客的任何平台收听《心理学谈话》的往期节目。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please subscribe and leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢我们的节目，请订阅并留下评论。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·韦纳曼（Lee Weinerman）制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频编辑是克里斯·康达扬（Chris Kondayan）。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。
